1: Jews in Jerusalem write to those in Egypt to keep the feast of the Temple's purification. A story of the sacred fire is told.
2: Jeremiah is said to have hidden the ark in a cave. The author explains he is summarising a longer work.
The author is frank about how he wrote.
3: A royal official comes to seize the Temple treasury. A heavenly horseman and two young men strike him down.
4: Jason and then Menelaus buy the office with bribes and promote Greek ways. The good high priest Onias is murdered.
Corruption from inside comes before persecution from outside.
5: Antiochus massacres the people of Jerusalem and loots the Temple.
God chose the place for the people's sake, not the people for the place.
6: The law is banned. Ninety-year-old Eleazar refuses even to pretend to eat pork, so as not to mislead the young.
He will not give scandal to save his life.
7: The mother and her seven sons
Seven brothers are tortured to death one by one, professing that God will raise them. Their mother encourages each and dies last.
A clear witness to the resurrection of the body and to creation from nothing.
8: Judas gathers six thousand men and defeats Nicanor.
God's anger has turned to mercy.
9: Antiochus is struck with a horrible disease and dies in agony.
The proud persecutor learns too late.
10: Judas retakes the Temple and purifies it, and a yearly feast is decreed.
11: A heavenly horseman leads Judas's army. Peace letters follow.
12: After a battle, the fallen are found wearing pagan charms. Judas takes a collection for a sacrifice for their sins.
A key text for praying for the dead and for the doctrine of purgatory.
13: The young king invades. Menelaus is executed. Judas attacks by night, and a treaty is made.
14: Nicanor is sent against Judas, befriends him, then threatens the Temple. The elder Razis dies defiantly.
A hard chapter from a time of terror.
15: Judas sees the dead high priest Onias and the prophet Jeremiah praying for the people. Nicanor is defeated.
Scriptural support for the intercession of the saints.
